## SECTION 1.5. BASE RATE & HISTORICAL PATTERN

**Step 1.5-2. Deviation from base rate:** My base case assumes growth decelerates 14%→7% by FY2030 and margin holds at 14.5%. The *bull* case (which the market prices) requires the low-base-rate outcomes (sustained 15%+ growth, 3,500 stores on time, durable 15% OI) to all occur. Three company-specific justifications that FIVE is *better than base rate*: (1) a genuine differentiating "treasure-hunt / destination for the KID" brand driving 22.7% comps and 25.9% traffic [Estimate, web brief]; (2) SG&A leverage from scale (SG&A 22.4% of rev, falling); (3) a real unit runway (2,080 → 3,500). These justify a premium to a generic discounter but **not** to the point the market has paid.

**Step 1.5-3. Base-rate shock check:** The market's implied success probability (pricing the bull case as base) is **>2.0x** the base rate for sustained high-growth/high-margin discounter outcomes → **RED FLAG, mandatory re-evaluation.** This is the core of the overvaluation finding.

## SECTION 3.5. SECOND-ORDER EFFECTS

**3.5-2. Reflexivity:** Positive — a strong stock eases capital access and talent retention (CEO Winnie Park's team). Negative — at 27x, any comp miss triggers a sharp de-rating (the stock already "sank after beating but warning of tougher consumer" per web brief). High beta to sentiment.

**3.5-3. Customer evolution:** Early-adopter "kid" cohort aging; LTV rises with the "kid in all of us" extension, but churn risk rises as the novelty fades and the base matures. Traffic (25.9% Q1) is the leading indicator to watch.
